    Title: "Verify Robust Rejection During Voltage Ramp-Down (No False Acceptance)"

    Title: "Verify Steering Angle Signal Continuity and Non-Stuck Behavior During <SIG> Operation"
    Method:
      Type: Dynamic
      Technique: Robustness/Stress Testing (Temporal Behavior)
    Pass_Fail_Criteria:
      Pass: |
        1. Initialize the ECU with steering wheel at 0° (sensor input = 0°). Wait 30 minutes simulating normal driving (CAN bus active, no faults).
        2. Simulate a slow clockwise steering input: increase the angle from 0° to 10° at 0.1° per second (100 seconds). Verify that <SIG_83> increments monotonically from 0 to 100 (1 LSB per 0.1°).
        3. Hold the sensor at 10° for 10 minutes. Then simulate release: decrease the angle from 10° to 0° at the same rate. Verify that <SIG_83> decreases monotonically back to 0.
        4. Repeat the test with a full lock-to-lock sweep (e.g., left to right) after 60 minutes of continuous operation. Verify no interruption or stuck condition occurs.
      Fail: |
        - The CAN signal remains at a fixed value while the sensor input is changing (stuck-at fault).
        - The signal does not return to 0 after the sensor returns to 0° (hysteresis or residual offset).
        - The signal exhibits step jumps > 5° (50 LSB) during smooth rotation (indicating sensor or ECU latch-up).
    Source_Complaint: ODI#11578760, ODI#11508600 (HONDA CIVIC – steering not returning to center, sticking after ~30 minutes)

- VC_Item:
    VC_ID: VC_SYRS.1089_A.NHTSA.2
    Title: "Verify No Unintended Signal Jumps or False Activation Under Transient Electrical Noise"
    Method:
      Type: Dynamic
      Technique: Fault Injection (Electrical Glitch / Sensor Disturbance)
    Pass_Fail_Criteria:
      Pass: |
        1. Start system with steering wheel at 0°. Inject a 10 ms, +5V spike on the steering angle sensor signal line (or a shorted sensor output to battery voltage). Repeat 10 times at random intervals.
        2. During each injection, monitor CAN bus for <SIG_83>. Verify that the <SIG>ted value does not deviate from the actual physical angle (0°) by more than 2 LSB (0.2°) during or after the spike.
        3. If the system detects a sensor fault (e.g., plausibility check), it may set a DTC, but the CAN signal must either remain at the last valid value or transition smoothly to a safe state (not an invalid range value).
      Fail: |
        - The <SIG_83> instantaneously jumps to an extreme value (e.g., 32767 or 1) or shows high-frequency oscillations that would cause undesired steering actuator movement.
        - The signal becomes stuck after the glitch or fails to return to the correct angle within 1 second.
    Source_Complaint: ODI#11536976 (HONDA CIVIC – steering wheel moves on its own, false activation)
